newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Students demonstrate after stabbing in E.Timor.
newsitem.headline: Students demonstrate after stabbing in E.Timor.

text.p: Disturbances broke out near the university and in a market area of the East Timor capital of Dili on Thursday after a local man was stabbed by a trader from another island, diplomatic sources said.
The sources quoting eyewitnesses in Dili said university students threw stones, stopped buses and beat up some non-East Timorese before university authorities calmed the situation.
A police colonel contacted by phone from Jakarta said one person was wounded and taken to hospital after an incident at the old market about 8:30 a.m.
He said one person was detained and the situation was back to normal.

Security was tight in East Timor ahead of the November 12 anniversary of the killing of at least 50 demonstrators in Dili in 1991 following a funeral for an activist youth opposed to integration with Indonesia.

The sources quoted local people as saying an East Timorese was stabbed by a trader from Sulawesi at Dili's Mercardo market. The wounded man was reported to be in serious condition in hospital, they said.
The students took to the streets on rumours it was a student who was stabbed, they said. University authorities later persuaded them to disperse.
There has been long-standing tension between the largely Christian population of East Timorese and Moslem traders who have settled in the territory.

Diplomatic sources said the situation was volatile although the military authorities had imposed tight security ahead of November 12. Eyewitnesses and human rights organisations have estimated up to 200 people died in 1991 in what a U.N. raporteur described as a "massacre".

Jakarta's troops moved into the former Portuguese colony in December 1975 and Indonesia integrated it as its 27th province the following July. The United Nations continues to recognise Portugal as the administering power.
Sources said the award last month of the Nobel Peace Prize jointly to two East Timorese had added an element of uncertainty to the situation.
One of the recipients, Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo, was quoted as having firmly told local people at a mass on October 26 that demonstrations, violence and burnings must end.
The other recipient, self-exiled activist Jose Ramos-Horta who lives in Australia, is demanding a referendum to carry the territory to independence.
